o.text:
Inherited from Old Anatolian Turkish آلمق (almaq), from Proto-Turkic *al-.
Cognates
Cognate with Old Turkic 𐰞 (l¹ /⁠al-⁠/), Turkish and Turkmen almak, Uzbek olmoq, Uyghur ئالماق (almaq), Kazakh алу (aluw), Kyrgyz алуу (aluu), and Chuvash ил (il).
Borrowed from Russian адвокат (advokat), ultimately from Latin advocatus.

Probably from Proto-Common Turkic *aš, but see also Persian آش (âš, “food”).
Compare also Chuvash яшка (jaška, “soup”).

glosses: tear (a drop of clear, salty liquid produced from the eyes by crying or irritation)

o.text: Possibly from Proto-Turkic *tam- (“to burn; to kindle; to become excited”). Cognate with Kyrgyz там- (tam-, “to catch fire”), тамызуу (tamızuu, “to catch fire”). Alternatively, same as Etymology 2.
Borrowed from Arabic شَاعِرَة (šāʕira). By surface analysis, şair + -ə.
